questions.question:
Some parts of a sentence have been jumbled up, and labelled P, Q, R and S. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.

Many retailers have invested

P. time and money into understanding its

Q. make them healthier so they can continue to be marketed

R. promotions work, and changing product ingredients to

S. complexity, refitting shops, trialling which healthier
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct sequence is indeed **PSRQ**.

 
 
• **P.** time and money into understanding its
 
• **S. **complexity, refitting shops, trialling which healthier
 
• **R. **promotions work, and changing product ingredients to
 
• **Q. **make them healthier so they can continue to be marketed
 
 
 
• This **sentence makes sense** as it tells a story about the efforts of many retailers to understand the complexity of making healthier options appealing to customers.
 
• **These efforts include** refitting their shops, testing out different healthier promotions, and even altering the ingredients of their products to make them healthier, so they can continue to be marketed as such.

When **we arrange the sentence** as per** PSRQ,** we get:* "Many retailers have invested time and money into understanding its complexity, refitting shops, trialling which healthier promotions work, and changing product ingredients to make them healthier so they can continue to be marketed."*

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The cat ate all the pastries.

options.text: All the pastries is eaten by the cat.
All the pastries were eaten by the cat.
All the pastries had been eaten by the cat.
All the pastries are eaten by the cat.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'All the pastries were eaten by the cat.'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **passive voice**, the subject and object in the sentence are switched.
 
• The object of the action in the active voice becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• In the original sentence, **"The cat" **is the subject, **"ate"** is the verb in the past simple tense, and** "all the pastries"** is the object.
 
• When converting this to passive voice, the verb** "ate"** becomes** "were eaten"** to **match** with the** plural form** of **"pastries".**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'**All the pastries were eaten by the cat.*'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• **"All the pastries is eaten by the cat"** uses "is", which is incorrect because "pastries" is plural, so it should be "were".
 
• **"All the pastries had been eaten by the cat" **is incorrect because "had been" refers to the past perfect tense, not the past simple tense of the original sentence.
 
• **"All the pastries are eaten by the cat"** uses "are", which is incorrect because it refers to present tense, not the past tense of the original sentence.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".

I felt that / I was be groomed / for success in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase containing a grammatical error in the given sentence is** "I was be groomed".**
 
• The sentence *"I was being groomed for success in the world"* is in the **passive** **voice**. This is because the subject of the sentence ("I") is receiving the action (being groomed) rather than performing the action.
 
• The** correct usage** should be *"I was being groomed".*
 
• In English, **when we talk about** an action that was ongoing in the past (a past continuous action), we use** "was/were" + present participle (-ing form of the verb).**
 
• So**, "was be groomed**" should be **"was being groomed"** to correctly indicate the ongoing action in the past.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *"I felt that** I was being groomed** for success in the world." *

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the correct indirect form of the sentence.

I said, ‘I’m not very happy at work.’

options.text: I told her that I was not very happy at work.
I told her I would not be very happy at work.
I told her that I had not been very happy at work.
I told her I am not very happy at work.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct option** for converting the given direct speech into indirect (reported) speech is** option 1:*** "I told her that I was not very happy at work."*
 
• When we turn direct speech into indirect speech, we usually shift the tenses back. This is known as "backshift".
 
• In the given direct speech 'I’m not very happy at work',** the verb 'am' **is in the **present tense.**
 
• **When converting **this into indirect speech, we shift 'am' back to 'was', the **past tense form** of the verb** 'be'.**

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is:* 'I told her that I was not very happy at work.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 **is incorrect because 'would' suggests a future condition or a conditional mood, which isn't present in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3 **is also incorrect because 'had been' is past perfect tense, suggesting an action that completed at some point in the past before something else happened. The original sentence doesn't convey this meaning.
 
• **Option 4 **maintains the present tense 'am', failing to perform the usual tense backshift in reported speech, so it's not the best choice.
